description: Create the Kiro University Challenge submission artifacts that demonstrate the 7 required lessons inside the GitHub repo, each referenced from a judge-facing writeup. The lessons: (1) Spec-driven development, (2) Steering documents, (3) Hooks, (4) Property-based testing (IDE only), (5) Powers, (6) Model Context Protocol (MCP), (7) Agents. Plus the two bonus lessons (Kiro Web/cloud sessions/cloud config, and packaging a Kiro Power). This feature adds .kiro/ specs+steering+hooks+settings, a property-based test suite in packages/shared, a packaged Kiro Power, and a SUBMISSION.md that explains how each lesson was demonstrated with file references.
steps: Create .kiro/specs/ with a spec that drove this project: .kiro/specs/digital-monster/requirements.md (EARS-style user stories + acceptance criteria for hatch/evolve, care, battle, chat-by-stage, save), design.md (the React+Lambda+DynamoDB+Bedrock+CDK architecture, matching what was actually built), and tasks.md (the implementation task breakdown mirroring FEAT-001..004 with checkboxes marked done). This demonstrates Lesson 1 (spec-driven development). Keep it consistent with the real code (stages, model mapping, evolution rule).

Create .kiro/steering/ with project steering docs: product.md (what the game is + core gameplay rules), tech.md (TypeScript monorepo, npm workspaces, Vite/CDK/Bedrock, the 'env -u NODE_OPTIONS' + no-network sandbox notes, build/test commands), structure.md (directory layout + where logic lives: all game rules in packages/shared). Add YAML frontmatter 'inclusion: always' (or fileMatch where appropriate). This demonstrates Lesson 2 (steering). Do NOT touch the workspace-root /projects/sandbox/.kiro — only create the repo's own .kiro.

Create .kiro/hooks/ with at least two agent hook definitions as JSON (Kiro hook format): e.g. a hook that runs the shared unit tests on save of packages/shared/src/*.ts, and a hook that reminds to update the spec/tasks when a handler changes. Use a reasonable Kiro hook JSON schema (name, description, trigger/when with event + file patterns, then/action with an agent prompt). This demonstrates Lesson 3 (hooks). Also add a short .kiro/hooks/README.md explaining each hook since hook execution can't be shown in a static repo.

Add a property-based test suite demonstrating Lesson 4 (property-based testing, IDE-only lesson): packages/shared/src/__tests__/game.property.test.ts using a SMALL, dependency-free, self-contained property-testing harness (write a tiny generator + runner in the test file, or a shared test-util, since fast-check CANNOT be installed in this network-locked sandbox). Properties to assert over many randomized inputs: (a) care actions never produce hp<0 or hp>maxHp or negative atk/def; (b) applyTimePassage is monotonic in stage index (never de-evolves); (c) evolveStage only ever advances by at most one index per single evolveStage call; (d) simulateBattle with the same seed is deterministic and always terminates with a valid winner and 0<=playerHpAfter<=maxHp; (e) reviveMonster always yields hp>=1 when input hp==0. Seed the PRNG for reproducibility. The test must run via 'env -u NODE_OPTIONS node --experimental-strip-types --test'. Add a comment at the top explaining this is a hand-rolled PBT harness used because fast-check could not be installed offline, and that in the Kiro IDE the property-based-testing feature would generate/condense these.

Create a packaged Kiro Power under .kiro/powers/ (bonus lesson: package a Kiro Power) demonstrating Lesson 5 (Powers) AND the bonus. Structure: .kiro/powers/digimon-helper/ with a power manifest (power.json or manifest.json with name, description, version, keywords) and a steering/skill markdown describing a reusable workflow for this project (e.g. 'add a new growth stage' or 'add a new care action' end-to-end checklist referencing the shared/backend/frontend/infra touch points). Include a README.md for the power. Keep the manifest shape reasonable for Kiro Powers (name, description, version, keywords, steering files list, optional mcpServers).

Create .kiro/settings/mcp.json demonstrating Lesson 6 (MCP): a workspace MCP configuration registering at least one relevant MCP server (e.g. an AWS docs MCP server and/or a filesystem server) with command/args/env and disabled:false, plus an 'autoApprove' list. Add a brief comment doc .kiro/settings/README.md explaining which MCP servers are configured and why (e.g. AWS documentation lookups for Bedrock/CDK). Use the standard Kiro MCP JSON schema ({ "mcpServers": { name: { command, args, env, disabled, autoApprove } } }). Use uvx-based servers as examples (e.g. awslabs.aws-documentation-mcp-server) since that matches Kiro conventions.

Demonstrate Lesson 7 (Agents) by documenting and configuring custom agents: create .agents/ agent definitions OR a .kiro/agents/ doc describing the specialized agents used to build this project (architect/coder/reviewer loop) AND how they map to Kiro's agent capabilities. Note: the repo already contains .agents/tasks/ (the orchestration state). Add .agents/README.md explaining the multi-agent workflow (architect plans in .agents/tasks, coder implements features one at a time, semantic reviewer produces the review files already present at .agents/tasks/task-digital-monster/*-review.md). Reference the actual review artifacts as evidence of the agent-driven review cycles (v1/v2/v3). If a dedicated custom-agent config format is appropriate, add it; otherwise the README + existing .agents/tasks evidence suffices. Make clear in SUBMISSION.md how this satisfies the 'Agents' lesson.

Create SUBMISSION.md at the repo root: a judge-facing document with one section per required lesson (1-7) plus the two bonus lessons. Each section: (a) a 1-3 sentence explanation of HOW the lesson was demonstrated in THIS project, and (b) explicit relative file-path references into the repo (e.g. .kiro/specs/digital-monster/requirements.md, .kiro/hooks/run-shared-tests.kiro.hook, packages/shared/src/__tests__/game.property.test.ts, .kiro/powers/digimon-helper/, .kiro/settings/mcp.json, .agents/tasks/task-digital-monster/2026-10-04-152533-review.md). For the bonus 'Kiro Web / cloud sessions / cloud config': explain that the project was built in a Kiro cloud/Web session against a cloud sandbox and is deployed to AWS via CDK (cloud config = infra/), and reference infra/ and README deploy section. For the bonus 'package a Kiro Power': reference .kiro/powers/digimon-helper/. Write SUBMISSION.md primarily in Japanese (the user is a Japanese speaker) with the lesson names matching the user's list; keep file paths exact. Also add a short pointer to SUBMISSION.md from README.md.

Note on lesson 7 naming: the user's provided list auto-translated item 7 as '通関業者' (customs broker), which is a machine-translation artifact of 'Agents'. In SUBMISSION.md, label lesson 7 as 'エージェント (Agents)' and add a one-line note that the official lesson name should be confirmed on https://kiro.dev/2026/university/ when lessons publish, so the judge mapping is transparent.
acceptance_criteria: .kiro/ exists in the repo with specs/, steering/, hooks/, settings/, and powers/ subdirectories containing the described artifacts (NOT the workspace-root .kiro)
A property-based test file exists and PASSES via 'env -u NODE_OPTIONS node --experimental-strip-types --test', using a dependency-free hand-rolled PBT harness (no fast-check install)
SUBMISSION.md exists at repo root with one section per lesson 1-7 plus both bonuses, each with an explanation AND exact in-repo file references
All new JSON (hooks, mcp.json, power manifest) is valid JSON
No changes are made to /projects/sandbox/.kiro (workspace root); only the repo's own .kiro is created
Existing shared + frontend tests still pass; no TS1xxx syntax errors introduced
verification: env -u NODE_OPTIONS node --experimental-strip-types --test packages/shared/src/__tests__/*.ts  (all pass, including the new property tests)
python3 -c "import json,glob; [json.load(open(f)) for f in glob.glob('.kiro/**/*.json', recursive=True)]; print('kiro json ok')"
Confirm SUBMISSION.md references each of the 7 lessons + 2 bonuses with existing file paths (grep the referenced paths exist)
findings: Created all Kiro University submission artifacts under the repo's own .kiro (workspace-root /projects/sandbox/.kiro was NOT touched). Lesson 1 specs: .kiro/specs/digital-monster/{requirements,design,tasks}.md. Lesson 2 steering: .kiro/steering/{product,tech,structure}.md with 'inclusion: always' frontmatter. Lesson 3 hooks: .kiro/hooks/{run-shared-tests,sync-spec-on-handler-change}.kiro.hook + README.md. Lesson 4 PBT: packages/shared/src/__tests__/game.property.test.ts with a hand-rolled, dependency-free PBT harness (mulberry32 PRNG + generators + forAll runner, 500 runs/property) because fast-check cannot be installed offline; asserts care-action stat bounds, applyTimePassage non-de-evolution, single-step evolveStage, simulateBattle determinism/termination/valid winner/HP bounds, reviveMonster hp>=1. Lesson 5+Bonus B Power: .kiro/powers/digimon-helper/ (power.json manifest + steering/digimon-conventions.md + skills/add-growth-stage.md + README.md). Lesson 6 MCP: .kiro/settings/mcp.json (aws-docs + aws-cdk uvx servers) + README.md. Lesson 7 Agents: .agents/README.md referencing task.json/context.json/FEAT-00x.json and the v1/v2/v3 review files; labeled 'エージェント (Agents)' with the '通関業者' mistranslation note. SUBMISSION.md at repo root (Japanese, one section per lesson 1-7 + 2 bonuses + quick-map table) with exact relative paths; README.md gets a pointer to it. VERIFICATION: all tests pass (42 = 36 existing + 6 new property tests) via 'env -u NODE_OPTIONS node --experimental-strip-types --test packages/shared/src/__tests__/*.ts'; all .kiro JSON valid (python3 json.load); every path referenced in SUBMISSION.md confirmed to exist. NOTE: fixed an invalid hex seed literal (0xbatt1e -> 0xba7711e) during authoring. No commit/push performed (orchestrator owns git).
